topic: Whether and how engineers should review AI-generated code
thesis: The public disagreement is not accountability versus speed; it is where human understanding should live. Review depth should follow a change's authority, consequences, and recovery difficulty.

sources.notes: Establishes the public framing only. Quotations and positions return to original sources.

facts.claim: Mitchell Hashimoto described a workflow in which different models planned, implemented, and judged a change.
facts.sensitivity: Do not generalize one workflow into a policy for every project.

facts.claim: Asked how he knew that workflow's result was good, Mitchell Hashimoto answered, 'I read the code.'
facts.sensitivity: Use the short quotation only; do not claim mandatory line-by-line review at every risk level.

facts.claim: Mitchell distinguished private AI-assisted work from submitting work that other people must review and maintain.
facts.sensitivity: Frame as an open-source responsibility boundary.

facts.claim: Robert C. Martin said he does not read agent implementation and instead uses specifications, unit tests, Gherkin, mutation testing, QA, metrics, and final verification.
facts.sensitivity: Attribute the method to him; do not present it as proven universal best practice.

facts.claim: Robert C. Martin wrote, 'I am the engineer because I am accountable.'
facts.sensitivity: Keep the quotation brief and visibly attributed.

facts.claim: Code review can find defects, build a reviewer mental model, synchronize team language, and make responsibility explicit.
facts.sensitivity: Present as a synthesis, not a measured four-part taxonomy.

facts.claim: Community discussions repeatedly divide around maintainability and system understanding, verification throughput, cost externalization, and learning.
facts.sensitivity: Do not claim the threads are representative surveys or attach percentages.

facts.claim: OpenAI reported an internal greenfield product with roughly one million lines, about 1,500 merged pull requests, and no manually written implementation code after five months.
facts.sensitivity: Call it a company-reported greenfield experiment and avoid universal conclusions.

facts.claim: In that experiment, human work shifted toward specifying intent, building environments, and creating feedback loops; human pull-request review was optional.
facts.sensitivity: Do not imply that humans did no engineering work.

facts.claim: Cloudflare reported using up to seven specialized AI reviewers coordinated into one review and selecting review depth by risk tier.
facts.sensitivity: Company report, not independent comparative proof.

facts.claim: Cloudflare explicitly exempts database migrations from its generated-file review shortcut because generated schema changes still require review.
facts.sensitivity: Use as an implementation detail of Cloudflare's system, not an industry standard.

facts.claim: Godot said AI lowered the effort required to create pull requests while reviewer capacity remained constrained.
facts.sensitivity: Open-source governance context.

facts.claim: Godot requires human approval and emphasizes contributors who can take responsibility for and fix their work.
facts.sensitivity: Do not call it a complete AI ban.

facts.claim: In Sonar's survey of more than 1,100 professionals, 38% reported that reviewing AI code required more effort than reviewing colleagues' code.
facts.sensitivity: Vendor survey and self-report; reserved for metadata or supporting notes unless narration needs one bounded statistic.

facts.claim: The c-CRAB preprint reported that evaluated review agents taken together solved around 40% of its human-review-derived benchmark tasks.
facts.sensitivity: Do not translate benchmark coverage into a universal bug-detection rate.

facts.claim: An observational study of 278,790 review conversations across 300 projects found that human reviewers contributed additional understanding, testing, and knowledge-transfer feedback.
facts.sensitivity: Observational result; do not make causal claims.

facts.claim: Aaron's operating judgment is that review depth should rise with a change's authority, consequences, and recovery difficulty.
facts.sensitivity: Authorial framework, not an industry standard.

facts.claim: Aaron defines a critical system by failure consequence and a system of record by authoritative truth; the categories often overlap but are not identical.
facts.sensitivity: Authorial terminology for this operating model.

facts.claim: Reverting code may stop future bad writes without restoring records, messages, access, or decisions already affected.
facts.sensitivity: Use may or can language because recovery behavior varies by system.

facts.claim: Shipping risk and learning value are separate axes: a low-risk change may still deserve deep reading when the goal is to develop engineering judgment.
facts.sensitivity: Normative synthesis, not an empirical learning-effect estimate.
